Ava: noticed an inconsistency today: API returned 200 with a successful payload when we routed to a smaller model for quota reasons, but console flagged a critical 'Quota routed' alert. Support confused.
Diego: do we have a schema for this 'landing' signal? seems we don't.
Rin: proposal: canonical landing envelope = (http status if error|ok), body subcode enum, headers for quick detection. Example: body contains "subcode":"quota_soft_routed" and headers X-Redwood-Landing: quota_soft_routed, X-Redwood-Reason: quota.
Liz (devex): console should read the same enums and show consistent copy + action links (billing / retry / change routing policy). keep copy terse.
Ava: for SDK behavior: keep 200 for successful content; SDKs should expose a structured landing object and treat certain subcodes as client-action-needed (e.g., quota_hard_limit) to raise an exception.
Diego: telemetry: emit landing_state on traces and labels on request metrics. add counters: landing_total{subcode=...}.
Rin: also differentiate quota-driven soft routing vs hard rejections: subcodes like quota_soft_routed, quota_blocked, capacity_fallback. list them in RFC.
infra-bot: infra-bot: Feature flag 'landing-headers-v1' toggled ON for canary at 2026-03-22T09:12:00Z.
Ava: QA checklist: header present on fallback paths, body subcode present, telemetry emitted, console mapping validated. I'll open RFC with header names, enum list, SDK mapping, and dashboard panels. Please comment if any strong objections.
